summary: This note is a short biographical sketch of Thomas Paine, an English-born writer who emigrated to the British American colonies in 1774 with help from Benjamin Franklin. It focuses on his role in the American Revolution through his pamphlets Common Sense (1776) and The American Crisis (1776-83). The note cites John Adams's assessment that Washington's sword would have been raised in vain without Common Sense.
one_line: Biographical note on Thomas Paine, the English-born writer whose pamphlets Common Sense and The American Crisis helped drive the American Revolution.
key_facts: Thomas Paine was born in Thetford in the English county of Norfolk.
Paine migrated to the British American colonies in 1774 with the help of Benjamin Franklin.
Paine arrived in the colonies just in time to participate in the American Revolution.
Common Sense was a pamphlet published in 1776 by Thomas Paine.
Common Sense is proportionally the all-time best-selling American title.
Virtually every rebel read or listened to a reading of Common Sense.
Common Sense crystallized the rebellious demand for independence from Great Britain.
The American Crisis was a pro-revolutionary pamphlet series published from 1776 to 1783.
John Adams said, "Without the pen of the author of Common Sense, the sword of Washington would have been raised in vain."
